assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the first controlled, non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons. The infinite-dimension limit gives a local self-energy, and the mapping onto a self-consistent quantum impurity problem is conceptually clean. It explains the Mott transition and the coexistence of coherent quasiparticles and Hubbard bands. Combined with density functional theory (DFT+DMFT) it became a working tool for real materials such as transition-metal oxides, f-electron systems and iron-based superconductors, a lasting methodological impact across solid-state physics.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar (with Krauth and Rozenberg) established the impurity-model mapping and the practical DMFT scheme. The three credited names are a natural and fair trio for the core idea. Others (Muller-Hartmann, Rozenberg) also contributed, but only credited names can be proposed.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent use, validation against experiment, and extensions (cluster DMFT, DFT+DMFT, nonequilibrium DMFT) make it mature. Recognition is timely. The known limitation that the local approximation neglects non-local correlations is a limitation of the method, not a flaw in the discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views a theory and method contribution as a discovery about nature or as a tool; Nobel precedent for methods in condensed matter is mixed.
Allocation of credit among early contributors (Metzner, Muller-Hartmann, Rozenberg, Krauth) beyond the three credited names is not resolved by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible, large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions turned spin-dependent tunnelling (Julliere's earlier low-temperature result) into a practical effect. It underlies read heads, MRAM and magnetic sensors, and is a direct sequel to the giant magnetoresistance prize of 2007. It is physically rich: spin-polarized band structure, interface electronic structure and, later, coherent tunnelling through crystalline MgO with symmetry filtering, which first-principles calculations predicted and explained.
assessment.attribution: The 1995 independent observations by Moodera and Miyazaki are the decisive first demonstrations of large room-temperature TMR. Parkin and Yuasa/Djayaprawira later contributed the MgO coherent-tunnelling enhancement. A two-person prize for the original discovery is defensible, but the MgO phase (Parkin, plus theory by Butler and Mathon) complicates a complete allocation.
assessment.maturity: The effect is thoroughly confirmed and has been in commercial devices for about two decades. Recognition is not premature and, relative to the technology, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should be limited to the 1995 discovery or extended to the MgO-based step, which would bring Parkin (credited, but outside my two-name selection) and theorists into the allocation.
Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may lead some members to see this as an incremental follow-up.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a tunable platform for flat-band, strongly correlated physics, with correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean carbon system, and led to the broader field of moire materials. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at a magic angle and experiment confirmed the idea. This is a rare theory-to-experiment success with large impact, and it touches the electronic-structure and correlation questions I know best.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the key 2011 theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators made the 2018 discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. The three credited names form a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration. Other contributors (e.g. earlier theory by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, and experimental co-workers) are not in the supplied credit, so allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Independent reproduction across several groups is strong and the field is large. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity and of the correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not fully stable. The discovery itself (correlated states at the magic angle) is robust.
uncertainties: Origin of the superconducting pairing is unresolved.
Credit allocation among earlier theorists and the experimental groups, some outside the supplied names, may be contested.
Possibly early compared with long-confirmed candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Angle-resolved photoemission turned the measurement of electron energy and momentum into a direct probe of band structure, Fermi surfaces, gaps and many-body renormalizations. Its application to cuprate superconductors (Fermi surface, d-wave gap, pseudogap, kinks) and topological materials has shaped modern condensed matter physics. It is the experimental counterpart of the spectra I try to understand through calculation, and its gains in energy and momentum resolution are a clear technical advance.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano, Shen and Johnson were each central in establishing high-resolution ARPES on correlated and superconducting materials. The three-person set is plausible, but instrumentation and photoemission theory are widely shared across groups and generations, so decisive contributions are diffuse.
assessment.maturity: The technique is thoroughly mature and heavily used, with results independently confirmed. Recognition is timely or late, though the prize would honor a method more than a single discovery.
uncertainties: A prize for a technique spanning many results may be hard to define as one discovery.
Credit spans many groups beyond the three names, including early photoemission theory and instrument builders.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Neodymium-iron-boron magnets, with Nd2Fe14B the highest-energy-product permanent magnet known, transformed motors, generators, hard drives and wind turbines. The discovery was of a new compound combining giant uniaxial anisotropy from the rare-earth sublattice with strong 3d exchange. This is a magnetism problem I understand well: 4f-3d coupling and crystal-field anisotropy matter. The technological impact is immense, which weighs in favor of lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (sintered route, Sumitomo) and Croat (melt-spun route, General Motors) announced the discovery independently in 1983-84. The two-person configuration is natural, though attribution may be contested because of company and patent context, and structural identification by others also matters.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of continuous industrial use and extensive characterization give very high maturity. The fundamental physics was clarified by later work. Recognition is late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers the work a physics discovery rather than materials engineering or chemistry.
Intellectual-property disputes and the roles of other groups may complicate a clean attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed the trapped-ion quantum gate, which made quantum computing with controlled physical systems a concrete experimental program, and developed theoretical foundations for quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions. The impact on quantum information science and on quantum simulation of many-body models is broad and foundational.
assessment.attribution: The two names are the clear authors of the 1995 ion-trap proposal and of long collaborating theory lines, giving a clean two-person configuration. Experimental realization (Wineland, Blatt, Monroe; Wineland was already recognized in 2012) separates theory from experimental credit.
assessment.maturity: The ion-trap architecture is validated by many experiments, though scalable computing is still developing. Recognition is mature for the proposal itself, but the longer-term outcome of quantum computing is open.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should combine theory with the experimental achievements in ion traps, which would change the allocation.
Proximity to prior prizes in quantum control (2012) and quantum circuits (2025) may reduce priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created a way to couple superconducting qubits to microwave resonators with strong coupling, dispersive readout and a scalable architecture. It underlies most superconducting quantum processors and gives a laboratory for quantum optics on a chip. The impact on quantum technology is large and traceable to the idea.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal and performed the first strong-coupling experiments. Choosing three of the four credited names forces an arbitrary exclusion (Blais) and a theory-versus-experiment decision, so the allocation is not obviously fair.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups confirm the physics and the method is used in industry. The 2025 prize recognized related superconducting-circuit quantum phenomena, so the committee must judge how distinct cQED is from that work.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recently awarded superconducting-circuit work may argue for waiting.
Four credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so allocation is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third class of collinear magnetic order, with compensated moments but spin-split bands set by crystal symmetry and no net magnetization. It is conceptually fresh, connects spin-group symmetry to band structure, and promises spintronic applications with antiferromagnet-like robustness. As a magnetism theorist I find the classification and the first-principles predictions appealing.
assessment.attribution: The 2022 theoretical classification by Šmejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth is the core, though earlier related proposals and spin-group symmetry results by others affect priority. The three credited names are a plausible set, but priority is contested.
assessment.maturity: Spectroscopic experiments on MnTe and CrSb have reported spin splitting within a few years, but the field is young and long-term consequences, including application impact, are not established. Recognition now would be premature.
uncertainties: Priority questions regarding independent earlier proposals and spin-group symmetry results.
Little time has passed for confirmation, and application potential is unproven.
